project: CSCO Interview Prep — Staged Quiz Game
description: An interactive, single-file (GitHub Pages friendly) quiz game built from the 300 Chief Supply Chain Officer interview questions. The 19 source sections become 19 sequential stages/levels. The player must clear each stage to unlock the next and reach the final level. Each question presents multiple answers with exactly one correct answer. Clicking the correct answer turns it green and shows a 'why this is right' explanation pop-up; clicking a wrong answer turns it red and shows an 'Incorrect, try again' pop-up with no explanation, and lets the player retry. On finishing the whole game, a personal motivational victory message is shown.

priorLessonsConsulted.summary: For this repo, the .docx resume is the source of truth; do not regenerate content from the .txt. Applies only to resume content, not the interview question bank.

The existing live site (index.html) is a single self-contained HTML file served via GitHub Pages at thalia2626.github.io/resume-/. New quiz app should follow the same zero-build, self-contained pattern for frictionless hosting.

userStories.title: One-command local launcher that opens the browser
userStories.description: As a player on Windows or Linux/macOS, I want to run one script that starts a local server and automatically opens my default browser to the game URL, so the game 'just starts' with no manual steps.
acceptanceCriteria: A launcher exists for Windows (play.bat or play.ps1) and for Linux/macOS (play.sh).
The launcher starts a local static web server serving the repo folder (preferring an already-installed runtime: python3/python, else node, else php).
The launcher auto-opens the default browser to the served local URL (e.g. http://localhost:8000).
The launcher picks a free port or a sensible default and prints the URL it used.
The launcher does not require installing new dependencies when a common runtime is already present.
Launcher runs from the repo root regardless of the caller's current directory.
Typecheck passes.
All validators pass.
